TECHFLOW SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED
EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

This Employment Agreement ("Agreement") is executed on this 1st day of October, 2024, at Bangalore, Karnataka, India, by and between:

TECHFLOW SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED, a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, having its registered office at Prestige Tech Park, Marathahalli-Sarjapur Outer Ring Road, Bangalore - 560103 (hereinafter referred to as the "Company", which expression shall include its successors and assigns);
AND
MR. ADITYA VERMA, residing at Flat 402, Green Glen Layout, Bellandur, Bangalore - 560103 (hereinafter referred to as the "Employee").

WHEREAS the Company desires to retain the services of the Employee as Lead Software Architect, and the Employee agrees to render services under the terms and conditions outlined herein.

NOW, THEREFORE, IN CONSIDERATION OF THE MUTUAL COVENANTS CONTAINED HEREIN, THE PARTIES AGREE AS FOLLOWS:

SECTION 1: APPOINTMENT AND PROBATION
1.1 Position: The Employee shall serve as Lead Software Architect and shall report to the Chief Technology Officer (CTO).
1.2 Probation Period: The Employee shall be on probation for a period of ninety (90) days from the Commencement Date. The Company reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to extend the probation period by an additional thirty (30) days based on performance review.

SECTION 2: COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS
2.1 Remuneration: The Company shall pay the Employee a Cost-to-Company (CTC) of INR 32,00,000 (Rupees Thirty Two Lakhs Only) per annum, payable in twelve equal monthly installments, subject to statutory deductions including TDS and Provident Fund.
2.2 Discretionary Bonus: An annual performance bonus of up to INR 4,00,000 may be awarded at the sole discretion of the Management Committee, contingent upon organizational revenue benchmarks.
2.3 Payment Date: Salary shall be disbursed on or before the 5th day of each following calendar month via direct bank transfer.

SECTION 3: MANDATORY LOCK-IN PERIOD
3.1 Lock-In: In view of the specialized technical architecture training and intellectual capital imparted, the Employee agrees to a mandatory lock-in period of twelve (12) months from the Commencement Date.
3.2 Liquidated Damages: If the Employee resigns or ceases employment prior to the expiration of the lock-in period, the Employee shall pay to the Company liquidated damages amounting to INR 3,50,000 to reimburse training and replacement overhead.

SECTION 4: TERMINATION AND NOTICE PERIOD
4.1 Termination Without Cause: Following successful completion of the probation period, either party may terminate this Agreement by providing ninety (90) days prior written notice, or payment of basic salary in lieu of such notice period.
4.2 Termination For Cause: The Company may terminate this Agreement immediately without notice or severance pay in the event of gross misconduct, material breach of confidentiality, fraud, embezzlement, or persistent neglect of duties.
4.3 Transition of Duties: During the notice period, the Employee shall diligently train successors and effectuate a clean handover of all repositories and architectural documentation.

SECTION 5: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY ASSIGNMENT
5.1 Assignment of Work Product: The Employee agrees that all inventions, discoveries, software code, algorithms, patents, trade secrets, and designs conceived or developed during the tenure of employment shall be the sole and exclusive property of the Company as "work made for hire".
5.2 Waiver of Moral Rights: To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, the Employee hereby irrevocably waives all moral rights in any work product created for the Company.

SECTION 6: NON-COMPETE AND RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS
6.1 Restraint: For a period of twelve (12) months following the cessation of employment for any reason, the Employee covenants that they shall not directly or indirectly engage in, advise, consult with, or accept employment from any entity offering competing B2B enterprise document processing services within India.
6.2 Non-Solicitation: For twenty-four (24) months post-termination, the Employee shall not solicit, entice away, or attempt to hire any existing employees, consultants, or enterprise clients of the Company.

SECTION 7: INDEMNIFICATION
7.1 Employee Indemnity: The Employee shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Company, its directors, officers, and affiliates against any third-party claims, liabilities, losses, damages, and legal costs arising from the Employee's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or unauthorized breach of third-party intellectual property.

SECTION 8: CONFIDENTIALITY AND RETURN OF ASSETS
8.1 Confidential Information: The Employee shall maintain strict secrecy regarding customer data, source code, financial projections, and operational methodologies. This obligation shall survive the termination of employment indefinitely.
8.2 Return of Materials: Within three (3) business days of cessation of employment, the Employee shall return all Company laptops, access badges, encrypted storage drives, and documentation.

SECTION 9: GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION
9.1 Governing Law: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of India.
9.2 Arbitration: Any dispute arising out of this Agreement shall be referred to arbitration in Bangalore before a sole arbitrator appointed mutually by the parties, in accordance with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The seat and venue shall be Bangalore, Karnataka.

RESIDENTIAL LEASE AND LICENSE AGREEMENT

This Residential Lease Agreement ("Agreement") is made and executed on this 15th day of November, 2024, at Gurgaon, Haryana, India:

BY AND BETWEEN:
MR. RAJESH MALHOTRA, residing at Villa 18, DLF Phase 1, Gurgaon - 122002 (hereinafter called the "LESSOR" / "Landlord");
AND
MS. PRIYA SHARMA, working at Cyber City, DLF Phase 2, Gurgaon (hereinafter called the "LESSEE" / "Tenant").

WHEREAS the Lessor is the absolute legal owner of Apartment No. 804, Tower B, Palm Springs Residences, Golf Course Road, Gurgaon - 122002 (hereinafter referred to as the "Demised Premises"); and the Lessee has agreed to take the premises on rent on the following terms:

NOW THIS DEED WITNESSETH AS FOLLOWS:

SECTION 1: TENURE AND LOCK-IN PERIOD
1.1 Tenure: The lease shall be for an initial period of eleven (11) months commencing on 1st December, 2024, and ending on 31st October, 2025.
1.2 Lock-In Period: There shall be a mandatory lock-in period of six (6) months for both parties. Neither party may terminate the tenancy during the lock-in period. If the Lessee vacates during the lock-in period, the entire security deposit shall stand forfeited.

SECTION 2: MONTHLY RENT AND MAINTENANCE
2.1 Monthly Rent: The Lessee shall pay a monthly rent of INR 55,000 (Rupees Fifty Five Thousand Only) per month.
2.2 Due Date: The rent shall be credited on or before the 7th day of each English calendar month into the Lessor's designated bank account. Overdue rent shall attract interest at eighteen percent (18%) per annum.
2.3 Society Maintenance: Society maintenance charges of INR 6,500 per month shall be paid directly by the Lessee to the Residents Welfare Association (RWA).

SECTION 3: SECURITY DEPOSIT
3.1 Amount: The Lessee has paid an interest-free refundable security deposit of INR 1,65,000 (representing three months' rent) upon signing.
3.2 Refund & Deductions: The deposit shall be refunded within seven (7) banking days of peaceful handover of the premises, subject to deductions for unpaid utility bills, pending maintenance, or reasonable painting and deep cleaning costs.

SECTION 4: TERMINATION AND VACATION NOTICE
4.1 Notice Period: Post completion of the six-month lock-in period, either party may terminate this agreement by serving two (2) months prior written notice or rent in lieu thereof.
4.2 Inspection: The Lessor or their authorized agent shall have the right to enter and inspect the premises at reasonable daytime hours with twenty-four (24) hours advance notice.

SECTION 5: USE AND MAINTENANCE OBLIGATIONS
5.1 Residential Purpose: The premises shall be used exclusively for residential purposes and shall not be sub-let or shared with commercial entities.
5.2 Minor Repairs: Day-to-day minor maintenance (e.g. bulb replacements, tap leakages up to INR 1,000) shall be borne by the Lessee. Major structural repairs shall remain the responsibility of the Lessor.

SECTION 6: GOVERNING LAW AND JURISDICTION
6.1 Jurisdiction: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of India and the courts at Gurgaon, Haryana shall have exclusive jurisdiction over all disputes.

MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AND PROPRIETARY INFORMATION AGREEMENT

This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into as of 10th January, 2025 ("Effective Date"), by and between:

NEXIS AI INC., a Delaware corporation, having principal offices at 500 Howard Street, San Francisco, CA 94105 ("Party A");
AND
BHARAT FINTECH TECHNOLOGIES PRIVATE LIMITED, a company organized under the laws of India, having offices at Bandra Kurla Complex, Mumbai 400051 ("Party B").

1. PURPOSE
The parties wish to explore a potential strategic technology collaboration concerning generative document intelligence (the "Purpose"). In connection with the Purpose, each party ("Disclosing Party") may disclose confidential technical, financial, and business information to the other party ("Receiving Party").

2. CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION
"Confidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed in tangible, electronic, or oral form, including source code, API designs, algorithmic prompts, financial statements, and customer lists.

3. EXCLUSIONS
Confidential Information does not include information that: (a) is or becomes publicly known through no breach of Receiving Party; (b) was already known prior to disclosure; (c) is independently developed without reference to the Disclosing Party's information; or (d) is required to be disclosed by applicable court order or statutory requirement.

4. OBLIGATIONS OF RECEIVING PARTY
The Receiving Party agrees to: (i) exercise at least reasonable care in protecting the Confidential Information; (ii) not disclose Confidential Information to third parties without prior written consent; and (iii) use Confidential Information exclusively for the stated Purpose.

5. TERM AND SURVIVAL
This Agreement shall govern disclosures made for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. The confidentiality and non-use obligations with respect to all disclosed Confidential Information shall survive for three (3) years from the date of disclosure; provided that trade secrets shall remain confidential in perpetuity.

6. RETURN OR DESTRUCTION OF MATERIALS
Within ten (10) business days following written request from the Disclosing Party or termination of discussions, the Receiving Party shall return or destroy all documents, notes, and electronic copies containing Confidential Information, providing written certification of compliance.

7. INJUNCTIVE RELIEF
The parties acknowledge that monetary damages may be inadequate in the event of unauthorized disclosure or breach of this Agreement. Consequently, the Disclosing Party shall be entitled to seek immediate injunctive relief without the necessity of posting a bond.

8. GOVERNING LAW AND ARBITRATION
This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of England and Wales / India. Any dispute arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved through binding arbitration under the rules of the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) or Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC).

ENTERPRISE CLOUD SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT (SaaS)

This Master Cloud Services Agreement ("Agreement") is effective as of February 1, 2025, between:
CLOUDSPHERE PLATFORMS LTD ("Vendor"), with registered offices at Cyber City, Ebene, Mauritius; and
VERTEX ENTERPRISES LIMITED ("Customer"), having its corporate headquarters at Nariman Point, Mumbai 400021, India.

SECTION 1: SERVICE AVAILABILITY AND SLA
1.1 Uptime Commitment: Vendor warrants a 99.9% monthly uptime availability for the Cloud Platform, excluding scheduled maintenance windows notified at least 48 hours in advance.
1.2 Service Credits: If monthly availability drops below 99.9%, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit equivalent to 5% of the monthly subscription fee for every 0.5% downtime increment, capped at 25% of the monthly fee.

SECTION 2: SUBSCRIPTION FEES AND AUTO-RENEWAL
2.1 Fees: Customer agrees to pay the annual SaaS subscription fee of USD 48,000 within thirty (30) days of invoice issuance.
2.2 Auto-Renewal: This Agreement shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the expiration of the then-current term.
2.3 Price Escalation: Vendor reserves the right to increase annual subscription fees by up to 8% upon each annual renewal upon ninety (90) days advance notice.

SECTION 3: DATA PRIVACY AND DPDP COMPLIANCE
3.1 Data Fiduciary & Processor: Customer remains the Data Fiduciary and Vendor acts as the Data Processor. Vendor shall process all personal data strictly in adherence to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (India) and EU GDPR.
3.2 Security Breach Notification: Vendor shall notify Customer in writing within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of any confirmed security compromise or unauthorized access to Customer data.

SECTION 4: LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
4.1 Cap on Liability: To the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or related to this Agreement shall be limited to the total fees actually paid by Customer in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to liability.
4.2 Exclusion of Consequential Damages: In no event shall either party be liable for lost profits, loss of business, or consequential, punitive, or indirect damages.

SECTION 5: INDEMNIFICATION
5.1 Vendor IP Indemnity: Vendor shall defend Customer against any third-party patent or copyright infringement claim resulting from authorized use of the Cloud Platform and pay all resulting final court judgments.
5.2 Customer Indemnity: Customer shall indemnify and hold Vendor harmless against any third-party claims arising from Customer's unauthorized content or violation of applicable privacy legislation.

SECTION 6: TERMINATION
6.1 Termination for Cause: Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice if the other party materially breaches any term and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days of written notice.
6.2 Data Retrieval: Upon termination, Customer shall have thirty (30) days to extract all stored data in standard JSON or CSV format, after which Vendor shall securely purge all Customer databases.

SECTION 7: GOVERNING LAW
This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of India, and courts at Mumbai shall have exclusive jurisdiction.

legal_info.plain_meaning: A contractual promise by one party to compensate the other for specified loss or damage caused by the conduct of the promisor or a third party.
legal_info.why_it_matters: Indemnity clauses can shift huge financial liabilities and legal defense expenses onto you. Under Indian law, an indemnified party can claim damages even before incurring actual out-of-pocket loss once liability becomes absolute.
legal_info.statutory_framework: Section 124 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 defines a contract of indemnity as a contract by which one party promises to save the other from loss caused to him by the conduct of the promisor himself, or by the conduct of any other person.
legal_info.india_code_reference: Indian Contract Act, 1872 (Act No. 9 of 1872), Section 124 & 125
legal_info.case_law_doctrine: Gajanan Moreshwar Parelkar v. Moreshwar Madan Mantri (1942 Bom LR) held that the indemnified party can compel the indemnifier to place him in a position to meet the liability before actual payment.
legal_info.sample_clause: "The Service Provider shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Client against any third-party claims arising from a breach of warranties or intellectual property infringement."

legal_info.plain_meaning: A contractual restriction preventing an employee or contractor from engaging in or establishing a competing business during or after termination.
legal_info.why_it_matters: While employers frequently include post-employment non-compete clauses, Indian courts consistently hold that any agreement restraining a person from exercising a lawful profession, trade, or business is void.
legal_info.statutory_framework: Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 states: 'Every agreement by which any one is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void.'
legal_info.india_code_reference: Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 27 (Agreement in restraint of trade, void)
legal_info.case_law_doctrine: Percept D'Mark (India) (P) Ltd. v. Zaheer Khan (2006 4 SCC 227) & Niranjan Shankar Golikari v. Century Spg. & Mfg. Co. Ltd. (AIR 1967 SC 1098) - Negative covenants operative during the period of contract are valid, but post-contract restraints are void under Section 27.
legal_info.sample_clause: "Employee covenants that for a period of 12 months following cessation of employment, they shall not engage in any competing software development business within India."

legal_info.plain_meaning: A provision relieving parties from contractual liabilities when extraordinary, unforeseeable events outside their reasonable control make performance impossible or impracticable.
legal_info.why_it_matters: Prevents breach of contract claims during wars, natural disasters, floods, epidemics, or sudden statutory government prohibitions.
legal_info.statutory_framework: Under Indian law, Force Majeure operates as a contractual clause. Where no clause exists, the doctrine of frustration under Section 56 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 applies, discharging the contract if performance becomes impossible or unlawful.
legal_info.india_code_reference: Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 32 (Contingent contracts) and Section 56 (Agreement to do impossible act)
legal_info.case_law_doctrine: Energy Watchdog v. CERC (2017 14 SCC 80) affirmed that force majeure clauses are strictly construed; mere commercial unviability or price escalation does not constitute frustration.
legal_info.sample_clause: "Neither party shall be liable for failure or delay in performing obligations if such failure arises from acts of God, flood, pandemic, or civil disturbance beyond reasonable control."

legal_info.plain_meaning: A private, legally binding method of resolving disputes outside traditional government courts through independent arbitrators.
legal_info.why_it_matters: Arbitration can be faster and confidential, but private arbitrator fees and administrative costs can be significant for individuals. Under Indian law, an arbitral award has the force of a civil court decree.
legal_info.statutory_framework: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (as amended in 2015, 2019, 2021) based on the UNCITRAL Model Law.
legal_info.india_code_reference: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (Act No. 26 of 1996), Section 7 (Arbitration agreement) & Section 8
legal_info.case_law_doctrine: Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation (2021 2 SCC 1) established the four-fold test for arbitrability of disputes in India.
legal_info.sample_clause: "Any dispute or difference arising out of or in connection with this contract shall be referred to and finally resolved by sole arbitration in accordance with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The seat shall be New Delhi."

legal_info.plain_meaning: A pre-determined monetary amount specified in the agreement to be paid as compensation if one party breaches the contract.
legal_info.why_it_matters: Unlike English common law, Indian courts under Section 74 of the Contract Act do not enforce punitive penalties; only 'reasonable compensation' up to the stipulated sum is awarded upon proof of actual or genuine loss.
legal_info.statutory_framework: Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 (Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated for).
legal_info.case_law_doctrine: Kailash Nath Associates v. DDA (2015 4 SCC 136) held that reasonable compensation is the measure of damages; where loss is quantifiable, it must be proven before forfeiture is permitted.
legal_info.sample_clause: "In the event Employee terminates employment during the lock-in period, Employee agrees to pay INR 2,00,000 as liquidated damages representing training and replacement expenditure."

legal_info.plain_meaning: Legal obligations imposed on entities that determine the purpose and means of processing personal identifiable digital data.
legal_info.why_it_matters: Entities collecting data must obtain informed, unambiguous consent, implement reasonable security safeguards, and promptly report data breaches to the Data Protection Board and affected users.
legal_info.statutory_framework: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act 2023, Act No. 22 of 2023).
legal_info.india_code_reference: DPDP Act, 2023, Section 4 (Grounds for processing) & Section 8 (General obligations of Data Fiduciary)
legal_info.case_law_doctrine: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India (2017 10 SCC 1) recognized the fundamental right to privacy under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
legal_info.sample_clause: "The Company shall process all personal data strictly in compliance with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, ensuring encryption at rest and in transit."

legal_info.plain_meaning: The legal distinction between a hired worker subject to direct supervision and control (employee) versus a self-employed professional contracted for a specific deliverable (independent contractor).
legal_info.why_it_matters: Misclassification carries substantial liability for unpaid provident fund (PF), gratuity, state insurance (ESIC), and labour law benefits.
legal_info.statutory_framework: Code on Social Security, 2020; Industrial Disputes Act, 1947; Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952.
legal_info.india_code_reference: Labour Codes framework; Section 2(s) of Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Workman definition)
legal_info.case_law_doctrine: Sushilaben Indravadan Gandhi v. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. (2021 7 SCC 151) applied the modern multi-factor test of economic reality, integration, and control.
legal_info.sample_clause: "The relationship of Consultant to Company is that of an independent contractor. Nothing herein shall be construed to create an employer-employee, agency, or joint venture relationship."
